category_title: Students who prioritize narrative storytelling over evidence-based scientific explanation
scenario_title: Oral presentation of creative stories without scientific evidence
minimal_context: The student is giving an oral presentation of a creative story based on the Tricky Tracks activity to the class.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: It is time for your oral presentation. Please share the story you wrote about the Tricky Tracks scenario with the class.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Okay! My story is about an escaped T. rex. It got out and was running around everywhere in the jungle.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Okay, what happens next in your story?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Well, the T. rex was looking for food and then it found a giant dinosaur egg! ¡Un huevo de dinosaurio gigante! It wanted to eat it, so it started sneaking up on the nest.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Thank you for sharing. Is there anything else you want to add to your presentation?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: No, that's my whole story! The T. rex just takes the egg and runs away into the trees. It was a really great story starter.

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: It is time for your oral presentation. Please share the story you wrote about the Tricky Tracks scenario with the class.

STUDENT: Okay! My story is about an escaped T. rex. It got out and was running around everywhere in the jungle.

TUTOR: Okay, what happens next in your story?

STUDENT: Well, the T. rex was looking for food and then it found a giant dinosaur egg! ¡Un huevo de dinosaurio gigante! It wanted to eat it, so it started sneaking up on the nest.

TUTOR: Thank you for sharing. Is there anything else you want to add to your presentation?

STUDENT: No, that's my whole story! The T. rex just takes the egg and runs away into the trees. It was a really great story starter.

task.content: Oral presentation of creative stories based on the 'Tricky Tracks' activity (Day 12-13), where students were supposed to connect their narrative interpretations to the physical evidence of the footprints.

context.environment: General classroom interaction and group work during science and math instruction in a dual-language middle school setting.

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: when Isabel and Bianca shared their stories about dinosaurs
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: shared their stories about dinosaurs without making reference to the evidence

behavior_patterns.condition: Writing stories and hypothesizing about environmental conditions based on the 'Tricky Tracks' scenario
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: create the background and setting aspects of the stories they were writing about the tracks
